title: Toledo, Detroit and the Sirens men now with Goldkette
summary: On a Toledo job he visited his brother in Detroit and found former Sirens men in the Goldkette band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: This is now 1925. I got out of school in 1925. So I worked with them for -- into the winter and we used to do some week stands at different places and there was one we did out in Toledo. And Toledo was 60 miles from Detroit, we got an electric car and went up to Detroit. Well, I had a brother there who was married and settled there-and I hadn't seen him for quite a long period. My oldest brother. I hadn't seen him in quite awhile. I thought I'd go see him but also the guys who were in the Scranton Sirens were working with Goldkette.

They had gone to the Sirens and now they were with Goldkette. There was Fuzzy Farrar the trumpet player whom I played with with one or two jobs with the Sirens and Itzy Riskin, the piano player who came from the south, and Russ and another guy by the name of Cooper. They were up there, and the Dorseys were up there, whom I hadn't met yet.
But you knew who they were.

I knew their work. They were in and out of the town and I was going to school. They were working with the Sirens, so unless I went around to see and hear the Sirens, I never got to meet them, but knew all about them.

Now then --oh, yes, I did hear them. They were with the Sirens at a house party at Penn.State. Maybe a year before or after, but didn't get a chance then to talk to them. Jimmy and Alfie were saxophone players.
